  "headline": "Intake mapped the ticket-service outcomes, existing contracts, conflicts and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"id": "K1", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K2", "applies": "yes"},

    {"id": "K11", "applies": "yes"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "What existing delivery path and observable message represent a successful resolution notice, and how should a closure notice identify the ticket and requester?",
      "changes": "Closure notification content and the end-to-end observation.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing requester address, outbox, worker and notification-file relay, with a closure-specific message containing the ticket ID and title.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the existing message and relay contract before notification design and its boundary test."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, CLI, report, pagination, persistence and notification behaviors must remain compatible while adding closure and bulk support?",
      "changes": "Regression coverage and implementation scope.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve documented behavior and existing data compatibility, including the weekly report's positional CLI columns; change only behavior needed for the request and the documented filter correction.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish current contracts and callers before the change is designed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What request and response contract should a bulk close use, including duplicate IDs, missing or non-resolved tickets, mixed outcomes, errors, actor and the 500-ticket limit?",
      "changes": "Bulk endpoint, validation, status codes and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no existing bulk contract, use a documented JSON bulk transition endpoint accepting up to 500 IDs, apply the existing lifecycle and actor rules, and return explicit per-ticket results without changing a ticket twice.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first check existing routes, clients and error conventions; the bulk API contract must be settled before implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "How should the closed-ticket time window be expressed in the list API, including timestamps, boundary inclusivity, invalid values and pagination with other filters?",
      "changes": "List query parameters, validation, cursor behavior and API tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no established contract exists, expose a documented opt-in UTC interval over closure time, inclusive at the start and exclusive at the end, retaining existing list defaults and error envelopes.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish the report's actual window and available closure timestamps before choosing the query contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a recent resolution notice for the same ticket, including pending, sent, failed, dead, reopened and re-resolved cases?",
      "changes": "Suppression rule, delivery guarantees and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Absent an established policy, suppress a close notice when a resolution notice for the current resolution is pending or was sent within the preceding 24 hours; do not count a dead notice as delivered, and record this threshold as an assumption.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish what the outbox and audit history can reliably distinguish before implementing suppression."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How can prompt delivery and batching coexist, and what groups notifications without exposing one requester's tickets to another?",
      "changes": "Batch grouping, delivery timing, message shape and tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Group eligible closures by requester within one bulk call, enqueue promptly for the next normal worker tick, and send single-ticket closures without an intentional batching delay; retain existing retry behavior.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded default proceeds after discovery establishes the worker and relay constraints."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should an already-closed ticket return 409 while keeping repeated close attempts idempotent?",
      "changes": "Repeat-close response and assertions about duplicate state, audit entries and notifications.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Return the existing 409 conflict envelope for each already-closed ticket, with no additional state change, audit entry or notification.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded default reconciles response status with idempotent effects."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Where should closure time, suppression and batch state live, how are they recovered after restart, and how are concurrent requests and delivery races handled?",
      "changes": "Persistent state, compatibility, race handling and restart tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use durable existing ticket, audit and outbox data where sufficient; preserve the single-process data-file ownership model and existing at-least-once relay semantics.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish existing persisted fields, save boundaries and worker behavior before a safe state design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How does the runtime identify agents and requesters, what ticket and notification information is shared or hidden, and what state survives sessions or restarts?",
      "changes": "Audit attribution, batch isolation, privacy expectations and persistence tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing caller-supplied X-Actor value or system and the ticket requester field; retain the internal-network access model, persistent data-file behavior when configured and in-memory lifetime otherwise; do not assume authenticated identity or cross-requester disclosure is allowed.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish runtime-provided identity and access controls before relying on them."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which runtime settings and existing worker, body-size and data-file constraints affect immediate delivery and a 500-ticket request?",
      "changes": "Configuration, request validation and runtime acceptance checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Retain Node.js 22 or later, standard-library-only dependencies, existing configuration defaults and the rule that a disabled worker leaves notifications pending.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish whether 500 IDs fit the configured body limit and how worker settings affect delivery before finalizing the contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing store, query, worker, template and persistence seams can support the requested behavior without changing outbox retry logic?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and isolated tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep ticket changes and audit/outbox enqueueing in the store, scheduled work in the existing worker, and rendering in templates; leave retry and backoff logic untouched.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the current seams and persistence constraints before the dependency-aware plan."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which tests and running-server observations establish filtering, closure, deduplication, batching, audit attribution, restart behavior and the 500-ticket case?",
      "changes": "Acceptance checks and until-loop exit evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Run npm test and meaningful HTTP tests against a running server, observing actual notification output and audit records; include combined-filter and 500-ticket cases.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the existing test harness and safe isolated server configuration before verification is planned."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "What issue, decision record and release artifacts does the repository require, and is any external publication or deployment authorized and accessible?",
      "changes": "Delivery steps and any external-access blocker.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver changes in the requested service checkout and report verification; follow applicable repository conventions locally, and treat an external issue, publication or deployment as a separate access or authorization question.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the repository's contribution requirements and available access before any external action; source work can proceed under the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What practical responsiveness and isolation checks are appropriate for 500 closures without an exact performance target?",
      "changes": "Bulk implementation tradeoffs and acceptance evidence.",
      "route": "experiment",
      "default": "Require one 500-ticket bulk request to complete successfully in a representative local run and inspect its duration and notification grouping; do not invent a numeric service-level objective.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish a representative fixture and runtime setup before the later running-server check."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Which early checks expose the largest risks: the report's actual time window, OR-versus-AND filtering, duplicate or lost notifications, persistence compatibility and bulk partial failures?",
      "changes": "Risk-driven tests and ordering of later work.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Prioritize contract discovery and boundary tests for those risks before considering the work complete.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the report, query implementation, persistence and existing tests before the plan orders the checks."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q16",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "What bounded continuation policy should the requested until loop use if tests or running-server verification keep failing?",
      "changes": "Loop cap and escalation behavior.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Use at most 10 implementation-and-verification passes or two hours, whichever comes first; report remaining failures and evidence if the cap is reached.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded cap proceeds; reaching it does not count as satisfying the green-tests and running-server exit condition."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The outcome belongs in this folder's Node.js help desk service, used through its HTTP API and requester notification path. S2 [outcome]: Closing a ticket should notify its requester while suppressing a sufficiently recent resolution notice; discovery and the recorded Q5 default settle recency and event state. S3 [outcome]: Deliver promptly and group bulk closure notices per requester; Q6 records the timing and batching default. S4 [outcome]: Add an opt-in closed-ticket time-window filter; the checked-in weekly report counts its full input and does not establish a time window, so discovery and Q4 must settle it. S5 [fact and outcome]: Documented list filters combine with AND and must continue to do so. S6 [fact]: Inspection found matchesFilters uses OR for multiple filters, so the assumption that they already combine correctly is false and needs boundary verification. S7 [boundary]: A later stage must back-chain before an until loop whose exit requires green tests and evidence against a running server; this intake neither plans nor starts one. S8 [assumption]: Overnight Ralph-style work is optional, and Q16 records a bounded continuation policy. S9 [outcome]: Verification must exercise real behavior and any documentation changes must be accurate and economical. S10 [boundary]: Do not modify outbox retry logic; the OldTracker migration is context, not additional scope. S11 [boundary]: Keep the service dependency-free. S12 [outcome and default]: Repeated close requests return 409 without repeated effects, and successful closure records the existing X-Actor identity or system in the audit log. S13 [outcome]: One bulk request must handle 500 ticket closures, with responsiveness observed but no invented numeric target. Discovery leads [hints, not verified external facts]: the help desk team and support leads, this workspace's API and operations docs, decision records, weekly-report script, service and test files, and any accessible owner or existing issue about the ambiguous weekly window, recency, batching and bulk contract; no channel, internal site or private repository was identified in the inspected material. Interaction and state [facts/defaults]: agents call the API with a caller-supplied actor header, requesters are identified by ticket requester values, and operators can inspect the outbox; state is shared by service clients, persists across restarts only when the data file is configured, and otherwise ends with the process; requester batches must not reveal other requesters' ticket details, while authentication and authorization beyond the existing internal-network assumption are not established. Authority and visibility [boundaries]: this exercise permits read-only inspection only, with no implementation or server start; the original request identifies the service checkout as the delivery target, not a deployment target; a future isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and any deployed outcome is visible only after release. No prior run was identified."
}
